principles: a mechanically confirmed setup is not an executable trade
a model assumption is not a source rule
a lifecycle run with substituted manual decisions is a model study, not a strategy backtest
the original strategy and the platform research portfolio policy stay separate
a research variant from a source the owner has not accepted never changes a contract status
no live activation, no orders, no broker

notModelled: a source cap per position (e.g. KK-001 30 %) is applied at the entry; a held position that grows above it is not trimmed
exposure scaling by market condition (manual or proprietary)
exit liquidity: participation is reported, not limited

modelAssumptions.reference: ACCEPT_AS_MODEL_ASSUMPTION (simulation only): every all-time-high box breakout of the research universe is taken
modelAssumptions.why: selection (DAR-Q12/Q14, B9-B11), volume (DAR-Q10, B3) and market (DAR-Q13, B14) are the reviewer's; a simulation runs only with them substituted, so it is a model study. Product records stay MANUAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED.

modelAssumptions.reference: AFTER_TOP_DAY (contract default of DAR-SF-BOTTOM-START)
modelAssumptions.why: start of the bottom search is SOURCE_AMBIGUOUS in #709 (VU-DAR UNRESOLVED); the DAR-Q2 wording (bottom only after the top is established) leans toward AFTER_TOP_CONFIRMED, the contract default keeps already traded lows; both readings are pre-registered

modelAssumptions.reference: the all-time high (DAR-Q9) is checked against the available split-adjusted history; records flagged ALL_TIME_HIGH_IN_AVAILABLE_HISTORY_UNVERIFIED are traded
modelAssumptions.why: the snapshot starts at the 2015 warm-up, not at the listing date; the contract sends such records to review, the simulation substitutes that review. No listing-date field exists in the snapshot to pre-register a verified-only alternative

modelAssumptions.reference: one raw cent in the split-adjusted basis of the arming bar (DAR-SF-ENTRY convention)
modelAssumptions.why: "a fraction" is not quantified (DAR-Q4/Q5); the reviewer may set another fraction per trade (DAR-MR-FRACTION). The level and the stop of an order use the fraction of the bar whose close armed it; the component study uses the fill bar: identical except across a split between the two sessions

modelAssumptions.reference: the buy stop is valid for the next session only and is re-armed at every close while the box stands
modelAssumptions.why: a resting order is the source (DAR-B5, DAR-Q4); daily re-arming reproduces it without a lifetime number

modelAssumptions.reference: PESSIMISTIC: an intraday trigger fill with a low at or below the stop on the same bar exits at the stop
modelAssumptions.why: a daily bar does not show the order of the trigger and the low; the contract derivation of DAR-SF-STOP-INIT is pessimistic

modelAssumptions.reference: after a stop-out a later all-time-high box breakout is taken again (DAR-Q11 reading, as the component study)
modelAssumptions.why: DAR-Q11 (CONTEXTUAL): new all-time highs can allow a re-entry; the decision is the reviewer's (DAR-SF-REENTRY)

modelAssumptions.reference: WEIGHT 0.10 of equity per position (platform model assumption)
modelAssumptions.why: no Darvas sizing rule (DAR-SF-SIZING manual; pilot buys DAR-B15 OPTIONAL). The stop one fraction below the top makes risk-based sizing hit the platform weight cap on most fills, so fixed weight is the reference

modelAssumptions.why: DAR-SF-RESEARCH-POPULATION: measurement convention, not a Darvas rule (DAR-Q10: no general minimum)

modelAssumptions.reference: a week is complete at its last session; whether the next session opens a new ISO week is read from the trading calendar, not from prices

modelAssumptions.reference: RUN_TO_TOUCH: ADX(14) > 30 on every bar from the start of the run to the bar before the touch (the contract component RAS-SF-PULLBACK); "rising" holds where the run crossed 30 upward

modelAssumptions.why: W-RAS97 rule 1 says "initially greater than 30 and rising" and rule 2 expects a turndown during the retracement; which bars carry the condition is not stated
